name: TwoTrees TTS-55 40W
tagline: 40W Ultra-budget diode with surprising build quality for the price
tldr: TwoTrees TTS-55 40W is the 40W SKU on the TwoTrees twotrees tts 55 line. TwoTrees undercuts Atomstack and Ortur on price while offering a usable 5. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Maximum cut speed and depth in the line: engraving remains strong at tuned speeds

priceRange.note: 40W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Shortest times of the TTS-55 line in our benchmark: ~12–18 min for a 10 × 10 cm photo, ~6–10 min for a 3 mm basswood square
Basswood up to 10 mm in our profile
Fill speeds of 45–110 mm/s, several times the 10W module's
cons: TwoTrees' own store does not list a 40W module for the TTS family: confirm the module's maker, optical rating and warranty
At $349–499 it overlaps with newer, faster 400 mm-class machines
Widest spot of the line (~0.10 mm) and more smoke on an open 300 × 300 mm frame
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 40W SKU on TwoTrees TTS-55. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Treat engraving and cutting as separate profiles. Push cut speeds only after test squares on your material. Compare CO₂ only when clear acrylic or all-day production enters the picture.

editorialDepth.advantages: TwoTrees TTS-55 40W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: Who makes the 40W module on a TTS-55?
faq.answer: Check the listing carefully. In October 2026 TwoTrees' own store offered 20W modules for the TTS family but no 40W module, so 40W TTS-55 listings may combine the frame with a third-party or older module. Ask for the optical rating (not electrical input) and who provides warranty.

faq.question: What does the 40W gain over the 20W on this frame?
faq.answer: In our benchmark, photo fills drop from ~18–28 min to ~12–18 min and the 3 mm basswood square from ~9–15 min to ~6–10 min. Our profile raises the basswood limit from 8 to 10 mm. The frame's 200 mm/s ceiling limits gains on large engravings.

faq.question: Is a TTS-55 40W a sensible purchase in 2026?
faq.answer: Only at the bottom of its $349–499 range. At that money, newer 20–40W machines with larger beds, air assist and current support are available. It makes most sense if you already own TTS-55 accessories or need a compact 300 × 300 mm footprint.
